video_title: Hyperliquid's Weekend Edge, TradeXYZ Rumors & Why 97% of Tokens Fail
gist: Blockworks Research analysts unpack a Hyperliquid HIP-3 SK Hynix liquidation event triggered by Leopold Aschenbrenner's levered AI/memory-stock unwind, present new data showing Hyperliquid's weekend markets predict Monday opens with 95% directional accuracy, and unveil a token-universe study finding the median crypto token loses 97% of value from its market-cap qualification point with under 2% ever beating Bitcoin.

themes.theme: Leopold Aschenbrenner's Levered Unwind and the SK Hynix Liquidation

insights.claim: Leopold Aschenbrenner's Situational Awareness fund ran roughly 4x leverage on a highly concentrated book of AI and memory-chip stocks (some positions over 5% of public float), and was margin-called during the recent NASDAQ AI-name selloff, forcing a one-block sale of the entire book to Citadel with Ken Griffin taking the other side.
insights.speaker: Luke (host)
insights.so_what: A single levered macro fund unwinding concentrated AI/memory positions can be a systemic-enough event to move an entire basket 20-30% in a day and spill into crypto-adjacent perp markets.
insights.quote: he he was running probably 4x levered on um on some of these names.

insights.claim: The SK Hynix HIP-3 perp market on Hyperliquid experienced a liquidation cascade because a single trader traded against an empty book during the pre-market session and printed a price 30% below fair value, and Hyperliquid's oracle (which stitches together pre-market, market, and post-market reference prices) briefly represented that manipulated print as the true price.
insights.speaker: Shondaanda (guest, Blockworks Research)
insights.so_what: Thin-liquidity regime transitions (weekend-to-premarket) are a specific, repeatable vector for oracle manipulation and cascading liquidations on HIP-3 markets that traders should watch around session switches.
insights.quote: within one print dropped the price 30%.

insights.claim: SK Hynix is the single most-traded HIP-3 market on Hyperliquid and was the first non-crypto asset ever to overtake BTC as the exchange's most-traded ticker, ahead of crude oil and silver.
insights.speaker: Shondaanda (guest, Blockworks Research)
insights.so_what: SK Hynix's HIP-3 dominance shows RWA/equity perps can out-trade native crypto assets on Hyperliquid, validating the exchange's push into non-crypto listings.
insights.quote: it was the first non-crypto asset to be the most traded asset on hyperlquid.

insights.claim: Hyperliquid liquidations are triggered off a 'mark price' built from three inputs -- the oracle price, a smoothing function, and the local order-book midpoint -- so when the oracle itself is corrupted by a thin or manipulated reference print, liquidations fire even though the true underlying asset price hasn't actually moved.
insights.speaker: Shondaanda (guest, Blockworks Research)
insights.so_what: Traders holding HIP-3 positions through low-liquidity windows (weekends, session transitions) are exposed to oracle-driven liquidation risk distinct from genuine price risk -- a structural tail risk to size for.
insights.quote: the mark price is basically the input of three things. the oracle the oracle plus some smoothing and the local midpoint

insights.claim: Trade XYZ voluntarily refunded over $1 million to traders adversely liquidated in the SK Hynix oracle-glitch event, even though its oracle technically reflected the manipulated underlying print accurately -- both analysts view this as the correct call because it builds trader trust and differentiates Trade XYZ's HIP-3 markets from other deployers.
insights.speaker: Shondaanda (guest, Blockworks Research)
insights.so_what: Deployer-level trust/refund policy is becoming a competitive moat within HIP-3 -- worth tracking which deployers backstop traders versus which don't when allocating flow across HIP-3 markets.
insights.quote: No, I think it is the right decision.

insights.claim: Comparing Leopold Aschenbrenner's blowup to Bill Hwang's Archegos collapse and Su Zhu's Three Arrows Capital collapse, the panel argues Leopold's episode involved no apparent fraud or 'crime,' unlike Archegos's CFD-driven losses (which cost prime brokers billions) or Three Arrows, so Leopold likely retains enough trust to raise capital and keep trading.
insights.speaker: Luke (host)
insights.so_what: Reputational recovery after a blowup correlates with the absence of fraud allegations, not the size of the loss -- a signal for whether a manager can re-raise.
insights.quote: Bill Bill Wayne's losses led to um billions in losses for some of the the primary dealers.

themes.theme: Hyperliquid's Volume Mix Shifting Toward RWAs

insights.claim: Hyperliquid's RWA (HIP-3) markets hit an all-time-high share of exchange volume last week at 63% of total perpetual futures volume on the platform.
insights.speaker: Luke (host)
insights.so_what: RWAs have flipped from a side feature to the majority of Hyperliquid's traded volume, changing what actually drives the exchange's fee revenue and HYPE buyback capacity.
insights.quote: last week marked an all-time high of RWA volumes at 63% of total per volumes on the exchange.

insights.claim: Pure crypto trading volume on Hyperliquid was roughly 50% lower in July versus a year earlier, and because almost no new crypto assets besides BTC, ETH, SOL and HYPE are worth trading, RWA/HIP-3 listings are structurally positioned to keep taking share of total volume even though crypto-native listings will periodically regain share whenever crypto itself is the 'hot' market.
insights.speaker: Shondaanda (guest, Blockworks Research)
insights.so_what: The addressable market for Hyperliquid's growth is increasingly traditional-asset listings, not new crypto tokens -- a reason to track HIP-3 deployer additions as the primary growth KPI over new crypto pair listings.

themes.theme: Trade XYZ Raise Rumors and the Hyperliquid-Deployer Symbiosis

insights.claim: Rumors circulated that Trade XYZ is raising capital, possibly a second round after an earlier round reportedly from Paradigm, sparking FUD that value is leaking away from HYPE holders -- but Shondaanda states he has zero confirmed information despite directly asking multiple contacts who would plausibly know.
insights.speaker: Shondaanda (guest, Blockworks Research)
insights.so_what: Unconfirmed capital-raise rumors are already moving HYPE-related sentiment; worth monitoring for an official Trade XYZ statement before repricing on the rumor alone.

insights.claim: The idea that Trade XYZ would leave Hyperliquid entirely is unfounded because doing so would require rebuilding its entire infrastructure layer from scratch and would amount to reputational suicide for a business built on Hyperliquid's rails.
insights.speaker: Shondaanda (guest, Blockworks Research)
insights.so_what: Traders should discount 'Trade XYZ is leaving Hyperliquid' FUD headlines as structurally implausible rather than a real risk to HYPE's HIP-3 volume base.
insights.quote: your argument would have to be trade XYZ is going to abandon every single thing that made it successful

insights.claim: It would be structurally easier for Hyperliquid to in-house or replace Trade XYZ's deployer role than for Trade XYZ to leave and rebuild elsewhere; Shondaanda's own April analysis argued Hyperliquid may be over-compensating HIP-3 deployers under a roughly 50/50 revenue split, especially as RWAs could become up to 90% of total volume within one to two years.
insights.speaker: Shondaanda (guest, Blockworks Research)
insights.so_what: If RWA volume keeps compounding toward 90% of Hyperliquid's total, the deployer revenue split becomes a first-order variable for HYPE's cash-flow-to-token accrual -- worth watching for governance changes to that split.

insights.claim: A standalone Trade XYZ token or public equity listing -- unlike the capital-raise rumor itself -- would be genuinely bearish for HYPE because it would fragment the investable vehicle for the 'on-chain RWA growth' thesis, unless Trade XYZ committed to routing its revenue into HYPE buybacks rather than its own instrument.
insights.speaker: Shondaanda (guest, Blockworks Research)
insights.so_what: A future Trade XYZ token launch is the one concrete tail risk to HYPE identified in this discussion -- a signal worth pre-committing a reaction plan for if confirmed.
insights.quote: if they were to ever launch a token or a publicly traded equity that would undoubtedly be very very bearish for Hyperlid

themes.theme: Hyperliquid Weekend Markets as a Price-Discovery Edge

insights.claim: In a study of every Hyperliquid market that traded over $1 million of volume during traditional-market closures, Hyperliquid's weekend/pre-open price called the eventual Monday directional open correctly 95% of the time whenever the resulting move exceeded 100 basis points.
insights.speaker: Shondaanda (guest, Blockworks Research)
insights.so_what: Traders can use Hyperliquid's weekend price action as a leading indicator for Monday's traditional-market direction on the underlying, ahead of the legacy open.
insights.quote: when the move was over 100 basis points, hyperlquid was correct, directionally correct 95% of the time.

insights.claim: Hyperliquid's weekend pre-open price cuts the median 'reopening error' -- the gap between Friday's traditional close and Monday's first traditional print -- by more than 50% versus not having that continuous price signal available.
insights.speaker: Shondaanda (guest, Blockworks Research)
insights.so_what: Continuous Hyperliquid pricing materially reduces open-price uncertainty for RWA underlyings, an argument the team is also making to regulators via a joint report with the Hyperliquid Policy Center for permitting 24/7 trading.
insights.quote: Hyperlid basically cut that reopening error by more than 50%.

insights.claim: Luke now charts Hyperliquid's and Trade XYZ's continuous NASDAQ market on Saturday mornings instead of traditional NASDAQ cash futures, because it is the only continuous, real-time price feed available while legacy markets are closed.
insights.speaker: Luke (host)
insights.so_what: A working analyst's actual weekend workflow switching to Hyperliquid is direct behavioral evidence that the weekend-pricing edge is real and already being used, not just theoretical.
insights.quote: I'm no longer charting like NASDAQ, uh, cash futures on Saturday morning. I'm charting the hyperlquid um and trade XYZ NASDAQ market instead

insights.claim: Hyperliquid's pre-IPO markets also price accurately relative to eventual listing prices, and the same principle applies to any venue that removes trading frictions (e.g., short-sale restrictions on some Asian equities) -- when controls are stripped away, the free market converges faster on fair value.
insights.speaker: Shondaanda (guest, Blockworks Research)
insights.so_what: Pre-IPO and restricted-instrument markets on Hyperliquid can be treated as reasonably reliable fair-value signals ahead of official listing, useful for pre-positioning.

themes.theme: Carlos's Token-Universe Study: The Base Case Is Near-Total Loss

insights.claim: Across every crypto token that ever crossed a $50 million market cap (robust to $100M/$250M thresholds), the median token has lost 97% of value from its qualification price, fewer than 5% of tokens ever outperform Bitcoin over a long window, and only 1.7% outperform Bitcoin among tokens with 24+ months of trading history.
insights.speaker: Carlos (guest, Blockworks Research)
insights.so_what: The modal outcome for buying a random liquid altcoin is near-total loss of capital -- the base rate strongly favors just holding Bitcoin over broad token-picking.
insights.quote: the median token lost 97% uh from the month it first qualified

insights.claim: Vintage/cohort ('underwriting book') analysis shows newer token launch classes default faster: 86% of the 2024 token cohort had drawn down at least 90% by month 24, versus 70% of the 2021 cohort and 18% of the 2020 cohort; overall 73% of all qualifying tokens eventually cross the -90% threshold, with a median time-to-default of 13 months.
insights.speaker: Carlos (guest, Blockworks Research)
insights.so_what: Token quality is deteriorating cohort-over-cohort, similar to a worsening credit-underwriting book -- newer launches should be underwritten with a higher default-probability prior than older ones.

insights.claim: The count of tokens worth more than $1 million hit a new all-time high in December 2024 and remains above 2021 levels, but every market-cap tier above $250 million peaked in 2021 and has never recovered -- the token universe has gotten wider at the base (via launchpad/pump.fun-style issuance) and thinner at the top.
insights.speaker: Carlos (guest, Blockworks Research)
insights.so_what: Rising small-cap token counts mask a shrinking large-cap opportunity set -- headline 'more tokens than ever' stats overstate the investable universe.

insights.claim: Centralized exchange tokens made up 32% of long-window Bitcoin outperformers despite being only about 2% of the qualifying token universe -- a 16x overrepresentation -- consistent with fee-funded buyback-and-burn programs being a real driver of relative token performance, though Carlos notes he did not formally test that causal link.
insights.speaker: Carlos (guest, Blockworks Research)
insights.so_what: Sector selection matters enormously within the small pool of outperformers -- exchange tokens with buyback/burn mechanics have punched far above their weight, a screen worth applying when picking token exposure.
insights.quote: exchange tokens were 32% of those long window long window bitcoin outperformers despite representing just 2% of the universe.

insights.claim: Factor analysis shows both high recent momentum and high recent volatility predict worse subsequent 1-month and 3-month returns -- the tokens attracting the most investor attention are the ones that subsequently underperform, i.e., outperformance mean-reverts rather than persists.
insights.speaker: Carlos (guest, Blockworks Research)
insights.so_what: Chasing recent winners in crypto is a statistically losing strategy per this dataset -- a concrete counter-signal against momentum-based token allocation.

insights.claim: Diversification does not meaningfully work in the current liquid token market because idiosyncratic-risk reduction is swamped by systemic crypto correlation across assets; a concentrated portfolio of one or two high-conviction token bets alongside Bitcoin is more sensible than spreading across 10-15 tokens.
insights.speaker: Carlos (guest, Blockworks Research)
insights.so_what: Broad altcoin diversification is a false-comfort strategy given crypto's high cross-asset correlation -- concentrated conviction bets are the better risk-adjusted approach per this analysis.
insights.quote: I don't think diversification makes sense in crypto today.

themes.theme: Fixing Broken Tokens: Disclosure, Buybacks, and Real Fundamentals

insights.claim: Since 2023, only three non-meme tokens have ever delivered a 10x return in liquid public markets: HYPE, Virtual (an AI launchpad token), and Mux Finance (a perp DEX token that Carlos notes 'isn't doing so well right now'), making HYPE's run a statistical outlier even within the small set of genuine outperformers.
insights.speaker: Carlos (guest, Blockworks Research)
insights.so_what: HYPE's 10x is a once-in-a-cycle statistical rarity, not a repeatable pattern -- tempers expectations for finding 'the next HYPE' among current small caps.

insights.claim: Disclosure and transparency frameworks -- such as Blockworks' 'TTF' transparency filing -- are becoming a real differentiator for token investability, functioning like SEC S-1/10-K filings for equities; the act of filing itself signals a team has nothing to hide, and projects like Metadao are building explicit token-holder-rights and alignment mechanisms to address the 'broken tokens' narrative.
insights.speaker: Carlos (guest, Blockworks Research)
insights.so_what: Projects that voluntarily adopt disclosure standards (TTF-style filings, vesting/incentive transparency) should be weighted more favorably in token underwriting as the market self-selects for transparency.

insights.claim: Even full disclosure will not save most tokens because many are fundamentally overvalued relative to their real financials -- Carlos cites an unnamed token with roughly a $100 million market cap whose annual earnings were only about $17,000 -- and crypto's low competitive moats plus aggressive points/airdrop growth tactics mean most tokens lack a credible growth story at current prices.
insights.speaker: Carlos (guest, Blockworks Research)
insights.so_what: Disclosure improves price discovery but doesn't create fundamental value -- investors should still expect the vast majority of tokens to be un-investable even in a fully transparent market.
insights.quote: a token announced it's like annual financials and they're a hund00 million token and their earning was like 17k, right?

themes.theme: Forward Catalysts: Metadao, USDC Yield, and HIP-3 Expansion

insights.claim: A Metadao decision market successfully defended an attempted $1.6 million drain of Umbra's treasury, with the attacker who tried to manipulate the market losing roughly $130,000 in the process.
insights.speaker: Carlos (guest, Blockworks Research)
insights.so_what: This is a live proof point that Metadao's futarchy/decision-market mechanism can economically deter and punish governance attacks in real time.

insights.claim: Carlos expects ICO activity on Metadao's permissionless launch platform (Futarchy) to accelerate through Q3, citing a recent pickup in ICO frequency over the past month.
insights.speaker: Carlos (guest, Blockworks Research)
insights.so_what: A resurgence in ICO-style launches via futarchy mechanisms is worth tracking as a Q3 crypto-market theme distinct from the launchpad/pump.fun style issuance already discussed.

insights.claim: USDC yield is set to begin re-routing to Hyperliquid starting August 26, and the panel argues the market is underestimating how material stablecoin-float yield will be as a revenue stream, monetized both directly and indirectly (via priority fees and arbitrage access on HIP-3 markets), citing Coinbase's earnings mix as proof that stablecoin yield can be a dominant profit driver.
insights.speaker: Carlos (guest, Blockworks Research)
insights.so_what: August 26 is a concrete, dated catalyst for Hyperliquid revenue/HYPE accrual via stablecoin float yield -- a near-term event to watch for its effect on buyback capacity.
insights.quote: USDC revenue that's going to start recruiting Hyperlquid on August 26.

insights.claim: The panel expects Hyperliquid's HIP-3 markets to expand beyond sports-style prediction markets into financial and earnings-related markets that trade alongside their underlying instruments in the same environment.
insights.speaker: Carlos (guest, Blockworks Research)
insights.so_what: Watch for new HIP-3 deployer launches tied to corporate earnings and other financial events as the next growth vector beyond RWA equities and sports betting.
